subject: Dedicated sizing kickoff: PeregrineAI commitment scenarios and traffic census
messages:
From: Chloë Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@peregrine.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena@peregrine.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0000
Subject: Dedicated sizing kickoff: PeregrineAI commitment scenarios and traffic census

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. To get our Dedicated capacity proposal right for PeregrineAI, we need a short traffic census and a couple of commitment scenarios from your side. The answers below let our capacity teams map to the right GPU mix (reserved vs burst), KV cache sizing, and expected latency SLOs. If you can fill what you have and attach a short sample of 24-72 hours of telemetry (timestamps + request_type + prompt_tokens + response_tokens + latency_ms), that’ll be ideal.

Quick ask (can be rough estimates):
- Peak sustained concurrency (P95 concurrent sessions) and peak instantaneous burst (P99)
- Typical prompt length (tokens) and typical response length (tokens) by endpoint (chat vs completion vs embedding)
- % of requests using tool calling / function-calls or heavy context ( > 2k tokens)
- Average session duration (minutes) and median tokens per session
- Desired p99 latencies (token generation or end-to-end) and what you consider unacceptable 

Proposed commitment scenarios (pick one or suggest your own):
A) Pilot: 50 reserved GPUs (mixed-A100/RTX), 2x burst pool — target p95 latency < 400ms
B) Growth: 200 reserved GPUs, 3x burst pool — p95 < 250ms, p99 < 1.2s
C) Enterprise: 500 reserved GPUs, regional replication — SLA + dedicated support

We’ll take your telemetry and map to sessions/occupancy, KV cache hit expectations, and an estimated monthly token unit cost per scenario. I’ve attached a short mutual action plan template (Peregrine_MA-Plan-v1.docx) — we can edit during the workshop.

If convenient, I’m free for a 60-min sizing workshop next week (Tue/Wed afternoons PT).

Thanks —
Chloë Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[chloe.martin@redwood.com]

[Attachment stub: Peregrine_MA-Plan-v1.docx (DOCX, 32KB)]
From: Samir Gupta <samir@peregrine.ai>
To: Chloë Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@peregrine.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 12:47:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing kickoff: PeregrineAI commitment scenarios and traffic census

Hi Chloë —

Thanks, this is great. Attaching a lightweight telemetry export that covers last 48 hours with anonymized request_ids. Quick answers inline below — please treat these as initial estimates; we can refine in the workshop.

- Peak sustained concurrency (P95): ~1,300 concurrent sessions during US evening.
- Peak instantaneous burst (P99): ~4,800 concurrent sessions for very short spikes (5-10s) tied to job-run completions.
- Prompt lengths: chat median prompt ~55 tokens, chat median response ~220 tokens; completion endpoint median prompt 12 tokens, response ~40 tokens.
- ~8% of requests include function-calls/tooling; ~2% exceed 2k tokens (long-context summarization).
- Avg session duration: ~3.8 minutes; median tokens/session: 280 tokens.
- Desired p99 latency: <= 1.0s end-to-end for chat SLO; p95 target 300-350ms. Anything above 1.5s is considered customer-impacting for us.

We’re leaning toward Growth scenario but want pricing sensitivity for 200 vs 300 reserved GPUs and a fallback policy for burst-heavy days.

Attached: peregrine_telemetry_sample.csv (48KB) — includes request_type, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, latency_ms by timestamp.

Cheers,
Samir
Head of Platform Engineering
PeregrineAI

[Attachment stub: peregrine_telemetry_sample.csv (CSV, 48KB)]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@peregrine.ai>, Chloë Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 03:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing kickoff: PeregrineAI commitment scenarios and traffic census

Samir — thanks for the data, this is very helpful. A couple of clarifying points from the sizing team before we build the model:

1) Burst profile: can you confirm the typical burst duration distribution? You noted 5-10s spikes — are those isolated or recurring (e.g., hourly at :00)? If recurring, what % of daily traffic do these bursts represent?
2) KV cache: do you have an estimate of session reuse (same user making follow-up prompts within a session) — that impacts cache hit rate and token generation latency.
3) Regional split: what percentage of traffic originates US vs EU vs APAC? We need this for regional tail provisioning and replica planning.

If it helps, we can run a short simulation with your CSV and return two outputs: (a) expected reserved GPU occupancy and (b) burst pool size required to keep p99 < 1.0s under your Growth scenario. We’ll include cost delta for 200 vs 300 reserved GPUs.

We can cover this in the workshop — I’ve penciled you in for Wed 22 Dec 14:00 PT, but Samir — if Wed is tight, propose a different slot.

—Marissa
Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Chloë Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@peregrine.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing kickoff: PeregrineAI commitment scenarios and traffic census

Samir / Elena —

Perfect, thanks for the sample and the notes. Next steps:
1) Marissa / Karthik will ingest the telemetry and produce a short Sizing Report (48 hours turnaround) with occupancy curves, recommended reserved GPU count, burst pool sizing, and an expected per-token unit cost for the Growth scenario and a 300-GPU sensitivity.
2) We’ll include a recommended KV cache config and an analysis of the ~2% long-context traffic — potential mitigation strategies (prefix pruning, batching, or routing to quantized higher-memory instances).
3) Confirm workshop: Wed Dec 22 at 14:00 PT. I’ve sent a calendar invite to the three of you. If procurement needs to join, we can loop them in at the start.

Deliverables: Sizing Report PDF, updated Mutual Action Plan (editable), and a short cost delta table for 200 vs 300 reserved GPUs.

If you want us to prioritize the p99 < 1.0s case, let Marissa know in the reply and we’ll tune for lower latency (higher reserved capacity + aggressive KV cache).

See you Wed —
Chloë
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[chloe.martin@redwood.com]

[Calendar invite: Redwood <> Peregrine — Dedicated Sizing Workshop (Wed Dec 22 14:00 PT)]
